approaches.name: Merge any pair until nothing changes
approaches.intuition: Repeatedly look for two overlapping intervals and replace them by their union.
steps: Stop when no pair overlaps; sort the result

approaches.name: Sort by start, then sweep
approaches.intuition: Sorting puts every group of overlapping intervals next to each other, so one pass merges them.
steps: Compare each interval with the last merged one
approaches.time: O(n log n) for the sort
pitfalls: Intervals that only touch (`[1, 3]` and `[3, 5]`) do overlap here: use `<=`.
Take the maximum of the ends: a long interval can swallow the next one.
Do not assume the input is sorted.

talkTrackMd: The key step is sorting by start; after that overlap is a local property. State the touching-endpoints rule explicitly and the O(n log n) bound.
